newsitem.title: USA: Timken sets Mexican bearing service unit.
newsitem.headline: Timken sets Mexican bearing service unit.

text.p: Timken Co said Monday it plans to establish a bearing repair and reconditioning center in Mexico as part of its Timken de Mexico operations.
The new bearing service unit will focus on reconditioning railroad bearings used in locomotives and freight cars.

"We applaud the privatization of the Mexican rail system," the company said, "and see our new investment in Mexico as a way ... to help the new owners and operators fuel a renaissance of the country's rail system.
"The privatization efforts, coupled with NAFTA, should result in rail freight moving freely between the United States and Mexico," Timken noted.
It said the flow of rolling stock between countries would mean that Mexican rail equipment must also meet the Association of American Railroads' specifications."

The new bearing reconditioning unit will be completely operational by year end. Until then, the repair needs of rail customers in Mexico will be handled at the Timken de Mexico complex in Mexico City, with the support of company reconditioning and remanufacturing facilities located in the United States, it said.
